findings.evidence: specs/lifecycle-workers/spec.md:19 requires "The token file location SHALL be read-denied inside the sandbox." In template/scripts/sandboxed_writer.py, build_profile builds deny_read only from DENY_READ_HOME, protected and platform. launch_sandboxed_writer reads the token with read_claude_token(config) but never passes the token path to build_profile. token_file is operator-configured and may sit outside ~/.config/dev-platform, for example /tmp or ~/secrets. In that case a sandboxed writer could read the token file. No test asserts the token path is in denyRead.
findings.summary: The spec says the token file location SHALL be read-denied inside the sandbox. The generated profile never adds the configured token_file path to denyRead.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/sandboxed_writer.py:320-323 (srt_launcher) only checks shutil.which('npx'). design.md says "or a resolvable `srt` binary whose `--version` matches; a mismatch is an explicit refusal". The spec's refusal when "the pinned sandbox runtime ... is unavailable" is satisfied only indirectly, through npx failing.
findings.summary: The launcher does not verify an available pinned runtime. It only checks that npx exists and relies on `npx --yes` to fetch the pinned version. design.md says a resolvable `srt` binary whose `--version` matches the pin is also accepted, and that a mismatch is an explicit refusal.

findings.evidence: proposal.md lists "denyWrite ... the push remote path when local". build_profile accepts extra_deny_write, but launch_sandboxed_writer calls it without that argument and has no code that derives the push remote. A local-path origin therefore stays writable only if it lies outside the allowWrite roots, which the profile does not enforce.
findings.summary: proposal.md says the profile denies writes to the push remote path when it is local. launch_sandboxed_writer never computes or passes such a path.
